newsitem.title: UK: EU working week ruling will hit small UK firms - BCC.
newsitem.headline: EU working week ruling will hit small UK firms - BCC.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce said on Tuesday that the EU court ruling on the working week would have most impact on smaller businesses.
"It's a significant problem but mainly for smaller businesses," said Ian Peters, deputy director general of the BCC.
He said a recent BCC survey showed almost half of Britain's small companies employ people for more than 48 hours.
But he said uncertainty may be the main problem.
"There are so many exemptions and uncertainties in the legislation. It's the uncertainty that's the key problem for small firms."
He said the government should be quite robust in its opposition, while keeping within the law, but that another row would not help the UK's relationship with Europe."

"That's one of the main reasons we were extremely unhappy about it being brought through the health and safety regulations. Yet again it makes the UK look the bad boy of Europe. It's an unreasonable position for the UK to be put in," he said.
On Tuesday the European Court of Justice rejected the main part of Britain's challenge to an EU law on working hours.
